items.q: Do I need to be a scientist to participate?
items.a: No. The Living Canvas welcomes scientists, researchers, students, artists and individuals with an interest in life sciences and creative expression.

items.q: Do I need access to a laboratory?
items.a: No. Participants without laboratory access can submit original creative works inspired by biological concepts and living systems.
Yes. Scientific videos, animations, time-lapse recordings and other moving-image works are welcome.

items.q: Can I submit more than one artwork?
items.a: Under the proposed competition rules, participants may submit up to three works, using a separate submission form for each work.

items.q: Can I submit work created with other researchers or artists?
items.a: Yes. Collaborative submissions are welcome, provided all contributors are appropriately acknowledged and have authorized the submission.

items.q: Can I submit previously published work?
items.a: Yes, provided you retain or have obtained the necessary exhibition and reproduction rights.

items.q: Who owns the copyright to submitted artwork?
items.a: Copyright remains with the original rights holder. Participants grant The Living Canvas limited, non-exclusive permission to display their work in accordance with the submission terms.
AI-assisted creative works may be considered if their use is disclosed. Fabricated scientific imagery presented as genuine research is not permitted.
Yes, with appropriate parent or legal guardian consent.

items.q: What happens after I submit my work?
items.a: Your submission will be reviewed, and you will receive updates regarding its selection status by email.
Details regarding submission fees, if applicable, will be announced with each competition cycle.

items.q: Can I contribute without entering the competition?
items.a: Yes. Researchers and artists are welcome to contact The Living Canvas regarding non-competitive exhibition contributions.
